UP and DOWN changed the board but the character stayed at the same position. The character is a 2x2 block (b on top row, S on bottom row). After UP, the character's shape changed from vertical (b at col 41, S at col 42) to horizontal (b at row 19, S at row 20). Wait, let me look more carefully.
Before UP:
- Node 5: color=S, pixels=2, boundary=[[19, 41], [20, 41]]
- Node 6: color=b, pixels=2, boundary=[[19, 42], [20, 42]]
So S was at col 41 (rows 19-20) and b was at col 42 (rows 19-20). This is a vertical arrangement: S on left, b on right.
After UP:
- b at [[19, 41], [19, 42]] - row 19, cols 41-42
- S at [[20, 41], [20, 42]] - row 20, cols 41-42
So b is on top (row 19) and S is on bottom (row 20). This is a horizontal arrangement: b on top, S on bottom.
Wait, but the character was already in this arrangement before! Let me re-check.
Before (after RIGHT x5):
- Node 5: color=S, pixels=2, boundary=[[19, 41], [20, 41]]
- Node 6: color=b, pixels=2, boundary=[[19, 42], [20, 42]]
This means S is at (19,41) and (20,41), and b is at (19,42) and (20,42). So S is a vertical 2x1 block at col 41, and b is a vertical 2x1 block at col 42. Together they form a 2x2 block with S on the left and b on the right.
After UP:
- b at [[19, 41], [19, 42]] - a horizontal 1x2 block at row 19
- S at [[20, 41], [20, 42]] - a horizontal 1x2 block at row 20
So b is on top (row 19) and S is on bottom (row 20). The character rotated from vertical (S left, b right) to horizontal (b top, S bottom).
So UP/DOWN rotates the character! UP rotates it one way, DOWN rotates it the other way.
And clicking on the character does nothing.
So the character can:
- Move left/right with LEFT/RIGHT
- Rotate with UP/DOWN
Maybe the goal is to move the character to a specific position with a specific rotation. Or maybe the character needs to "fit" into a specific shape on the bridge.

Wait, let me reconsider the whole game. The bridge extends with each action. Maybe the bridge is not a progress bar but actually part of the puzzle. The character moves along the bridge, and the goal is to reach the end.
But the character is already at the right end of the bridge. Maybe I need to extend the bridge further by taking more actions, and then move the character to the new end.

print("\n=== BRIDGE ===")
for r in range(17, 23):
    print(f"Row {r}: {lines[r][10:60]}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
